name: ip
description: The iproute2 tool for addresses, links, routes, neighbours and network namespaces — the modern replacement for ifconfig and route.

commands.explanation: Every interface and its IPv4 and IPv6 addresses (short for ip address show).

commands.example: sudo ip addr add 10.10.14.5/24 dev eth0
commands.explanation: Adds an address (not persistent across reboots).

commands.example: sudo ip addr del 10.10.14.5/24 dev eth0

commands.explanation: Interfaces, their state and MAC addresses.

commands.example: sudo ip link set eth0 up
commands.explanation: Brings an interface up; use down to disable it.

commands.command: sudo ip link set dev <iface> address <mac>
commands.example: sudo ip link set dev wlan0 address 02:11:22:33:44:55
commands.explanation: Changes the MAC address (bring the interface down first).
Packet, byte, error and drop counters.
The routing table; the default route shows your gateway.
Which interface, source address and gateway the kernel would use to reach an address.
Adds a static route — common when pivoting into internal networks.
The ARP/NDP cache: nearby hosts this machine has talked to.
Network namespaces, used by containers and for isolated testing.

commands.example: sudo ip netns exec lab ip a
commands.explanation: Runs a command inside a namespace.
